lesson.title: The shortest way
lesson.subtitle: Add up the roads, settle the nearest first, plan again when a road closes

video.title: The shortest way
video.format_note: Animated explainer, 16:9, flat Darsi colours on paper-grey backgrounds. Narration in the lesson language; captions as separate files, never burned in.
cast: Mr Okafor Eze — Grade 8 science teacher, Nigeria (main character)
Ms Salma Haddad — secondary maths teacher (cameo)
Ms Amina Bello — primary teacher, Nigeria (cameo)
Narrator — the Darsi voice (warm, peer to peer)

scenes.visual: Mr Okafor at the wheel of an old car, rain on the windscreen, a road sign: Bridge closed.
scenes.animation: Rain streaks; the sign swings into view; Mr Okafor frowns at a paper map.
scenes.narration: Heavy rain last night, and the bridge on my usual road to school is under water. I always drive through Kesi and Mina. Which way is the shortest now?

scenes.visual: Title card with the Darsi mark and the Optimization track chip.
scenes.animation: Mark pops in; title slides up.
scenes.narration: Today: the shortest way, and a sure method to find it.

scenes.visual: A clean map: eight dots joined by roads, each road labelled with kilometres.
scenes.animation: Dots pop in, roads draw between them, numbers appear on the roads.
scenes.narration: Draw the problem as a map: places are dots, roads are lines, and each road has its length. Here there are a home, six villages and the school. A way’s length is just its roads added up.

scenes.visual: Two routes highlighted on the map: a straight-looking one through Bora, a bendy one through Tala, Kesi and Mina.
scenes.animation: Each route lights up as its numbers are added; the totals pop.
scenes.narration: The road through Bora looks the straightest: five kilometres, then ten. That’s fifteen. The winding way through Tala, Kesi and Mina is four, three, two and four. That’s only thirteen.

scenes.visual: Numbered steps beside the map; home glows with a 0.
scenes.animation: Steps appear one by one as they are said.
scenes.narration: To be sure, use a method Edsger Dijkstra found in nineteen fifty-six. Every place gets a number: the shortest way found so far, and home starts at zero. Each turn, settle the waiting place with the smallest number, because nothing can beat it now. Then its roads may lower its neighbours’ numbers.

scenes.visual: The map again: each settled village turns solid, its number circled.
scenes.animation: Numbers update on the map as each village is settled.
scenes.narration: From home, the roads give Tala four, Bora five and Rubi six. Settle Tala, and Kesi gets seven. Settle Bora, then Rubi, then Kesi, and Mina drops to nine. Settle Mina, and the school gets thirteen.

scenes.visual: Blue water flows outwards along the roads from home, reaching villages one after another.
scenes.animation: Water lines grow along the roads; villages light up as the water arrives.
scenes.narration: Picture water spreading out from your home along every road at the same speed. It reaches the nearest places first. The first time it reaches the school, it came the shortest way.

scenes.visual: Ms Salma points at two waiting villages on the map. Three answer cards drop in.
scenes.animation: Cards bounce in one by one.
scenes.narration: Quick check! Bora has five and Kesi has seven, and both are waiting. Which do you settle next?

scenes.visual: Bora gets a lock and a check badge; a phone with a map app appears beside it.
scenes.animation: Check badge pops; the phone slides in.
scenes.narration: Bora, the smallest number. Any other way to Bora would pass a place that is already farther, so five is final. That’s why the method never has to go back. Map apps and delivery vans use faster versions of it every second.

scenes.visual: The bridge between Kesi and Mina turns red with waves; the new route through Rubi and Sana lights up.
scenes.animation: The bridge fades out; the new route draws itself.
scenes.narration: Now flood the bridge between Kesi and Mina, and run the same method again. The shortest way becomes Home, Rubi, Sana, School: fourteen kilometres. The shortest way depends on today’s map, so plan again when a road closes.

scenes.visual: Children walking from different villages; a small footbridge being sketched over a river.
scenes.animation: Each village shows its distance; the farthest one is circled.
scenes.narration: Every family has its own shortest way, and some are long. Before the council builds a footbridge, the school can measure each village’s shortest way. Then ask: whose walk gets shorter, and who still walks the farthest?

scenes.visual: A phone with the lab: the village map, numbers in circles, a finger tapping villages.
scenes.animation: Villages settle one by one; the shortest way lights up.
scenes.on_screen_text: App lab: The shortest way to school
scenes.narration: In the app, find the shortest way yourself. Tap Home, then always tap the waiting village with the smallest number, until the school is settled. Then flood the bridge and find the new way.

scenes.visual: Amina traces the straight road through Bora with her finger. Three answer cards appear.
scenes.narration: Your turn. The road through Bora looks the straightest of all. Is it the shortest way to school?

scenes.visual: Summary lines and an orange takeaway bar.
scenes.animation: Lines tick in; the takeaway slides up.
scenes.narration: No: fifteen kilometres, against thirteen through Tala, Kesi and Mina. Remember: draw the map with road lengths and add them up. Settle the smallest waiting number first. And when a road closes, plan again.

scenes.visual: Pupils on a chalk map in the schoolyard, holding number cards; Mr Okafor watches.
scenes.animation: Cards flip to new numbers; one pupil steps forward.
scenes.narration: Try it in class tomorrow: chalk a map on the playground, with villages, roads and their lengths. Pupils stand on the villages with number cards and settle the smallest number each turn. Then close a road, and find the new shortest way together.

checkpoints.prompt: Bora has 5 km and Kesi has 7 km; both are waiting. Which do you settle next?

options.text: Kesi: it’s closer to the school
Bora: it has the smallest number

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — settle the smallest number first. Nothing can beat 5 km to Bora now, so its number is final.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — always settle the waiting place with the smallest number: Bora, 5 km. That’s what makes the method sure.

checkpoints.prompt: The road through Bora looks the straightest. Is it the shortest way to school?

options.text: Yes: straight roads are always shortest
No: through Tala, Kesi and Mina adds up to less
Only when the bridge is flooded

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — through Bora is 5 + 10 = 15 km; through Tala, Kesi and Mina is 4 + 3 + 2 + 4 = 13 km.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — add up the roads: through Bora is 15 km, through Tala, Kesi and Mina only 13. Even with the bridge flooded, Bora (15) loses to Rubi and Sana (14).
